title: OAuth SSO ATO: The Persistent Backdoor
description: Exploit a flawed OAuth implementation to permanently hijack another user's account by chaining a paywall bypass and an unverified email change.
objective: Take over the admin account and retrieve the flag hidden in the billing dashboard.
hints: 1. Register using the Google SSO button with the email: `attacker@gmail.com`. Standard registration is blocked.
2. Once logged in, go to Account Settings and set a new password for the account.
3. In Account Settings, change your email to `victim@hole.local`. Notice that no verification link is sent, but the password you just set is now tied to this new email!
4. Log out. Now, pretend you are the victim. Try to sign up with Google SSO using `victim@hole.local`. It will fail, saying the account already exists.
5. As the victim, go to Forgot Password and enter `victim@hole.local`. Complete the OTP process (enter any 6 digits) and reset the password to something new. Log in to verify.

6. Now, act as the attacker again. Go to the login page, click 'Sign in with Google', and enter your original `attacker@gmail.com` address. You will be logged straight into the victim's account, bypassing their new password, and the flag will be revealed!

commands.run: docker rm -f hole-oauth-lab 2>/dev/null; docker run --rm --name hole-oauth-lab -d -p 3000:3000 holeworkstation/hole-lab-oauth-ato:latest
